newsitem.title: USA: Morton auto sector hit by high costs.
newsitem.headline: Morton auto sector hit by high costs.

text.p: Morton International Inc said Thursday fiscal second quarter sales in its automotive products business topped its expectations, but higher freight and manufacturing costs cut into operating margins.
Morton said operating earnings from its airbags fell 15 percent.

"Sales growth for Morton's Automotive Safety Products was above our expectations for the second quarter as sideimpact airbags and additional business Morton picked up offest sizable price declines," Morton chairman and chief executive S. Jay Stewart said in a statement.

"However, we continue to struggle with higher freight and manufacturing costs to meet the additional demand and those higher costs have again brought down the operating margins for the business," Stewart said.
Morton, which during the quarter announced it signed a definitive agreement to merge its airbag business with Sweden's Autoliv, said it still expects the transaction to close in March or April.
Earlier, the company reported second quarter earnings for the quarter of $0.61 a share versus $0.66 last year.
Morton's salt business showed improvement, the company said, despite tough comparisons for ice control salt. And specialty cheimicals saw a 14 percent improvement in operating earnings on flat sales.
